神经冲动的产生和传导: Generation and Conduction of Nerve Impulses
静息 K⁺ 外流 · 兴奋 Na⁺ 内流: Resting: K⁺ flows out · Excited: Na⁺ flows in
发令枪响后 0.1 s 内起跑就算抢跑（教材 p.27）——兴奋在身体里怎样「跑: Starting within 0.1 s of the gun counts as a false start (textbook p.27). How does excitation "run" through the body?
K⁺ 外流 · 内负外正: K⁺ out · negative inside, positive outside
Na⁺ 内流 · 内正外负: Na⁺ in · positive inside, negative outside
一段轴突、两个微电极接到同一台电表: A section of axon with two microelectrodes connected to one meter
磷脂双分子层上的 K⁺ 通道与 Na⁺ 通道: K⁺ channels and Na⁺ channels in the phospholipid bilayer
突触小体、突触间隙与突触后膜上的受体: Synaptic knob, synaptic cleft and receptors on the postsynaptic membrane
刺激神经的一端，电表指针会怎么动？: Stimulate one end of the nerve. How will the meter needle move?
把「电刺激」拨到「刺激中」，盯住电表: Switch "Electrical stimulus" to "Stimulating" and watch the meter
指针先往负的一侧偏（a 处膜外变负电位），接着回零；随后 b 处再偏一次，方向相: The needle first swings to the negative side (the outside of the membrane at a becomes negative), then returns to zero; then it swings again for b, in the opposite (positive) direction
静息时电表没有测出电位变化，说明神经表面各处电位相等。: At rest the meter detects no potential change, showing the nerve surface is at the same potential everywhere.
刺激左端后，靠近刺激端的 a 处先变为负电位，接着恢复正电位。: After stimulating the left end, point a near the stimulus first becomes negative, then returns to positive.
随后另一电极 b 处变为负电位，接着又恢复为正电位。: Then the other electrode at b becomes negative, then returns to positive.
去掉两个电极分开放：只会看到「一起偏」，看不出「先 a 后 b」。: Without the two electrodes placed apart, you'd only see "both deflect together", not "first a, then b".
电表只在两点电位不同时才偏：先 a 后 b，说明兴奋是「走过去」的。: The meter only deflects when the two points differ in potential: first a, then b, showing that excitation "travels".
兴奋是以电信号的形式沿着神经纤维传导的，这种电信号也叫神经冲动。: Excitation is conducted along nerve fibers as an electrical signal, also called a nerve impulse.
没有刺激时，膜内外为什么是内负外正？: Without a stimulus, why is the membrane negative inside and positive outside?
看几秒：数一数膜上哪个通道开着、离子往哪边走: Watch for a few seconds: count which channels on the membrane are open and which way the ions move
K⁺ 通道开着，K⁺ 不断从膜内流向膜外；膜电位稳在 −70 mV（课件设定），: K⁺ channels are open and K⁺ keeps flowing from inside to outside; the membrane potential holds at −70 mV (lesson setting), with "−" on the inside and "+" on the outside
静息：K⁺ 外流 → 内负外正: Resting: K⁺ flows out → negative inside, positive outside
膜主要对 K⁺ 有通透性: The membrane is mainly permeable to K⁺
细胞外的 Na⁺ 浓度比膜内高，K⁺ 浓度比膜内低。: The Na⁺ concentration outside the cell is higher than inside, and the K⁺ concentration is lower.
静息时膜主要对 K⁺ 有通透性，造成 K⁺ 外流。: At rest the membrane is mainly permeable to K⁺, so K⁺ flows out.
K⁺ 外流使膜外阳离子浓度高于膜内，膜两侧表现为内负外正，即静息电位。: K⁺ outflow makes the cation concentration outside higher than inside, so the membrane is negative inside and positive outside: the resting potential.
去掉 K⁺ 通道：就说不出「内负外正」是怎么来的，只能背结论。: Without K⁺ channels, you can't explain where "negative inside, positive outside" comes from and can only memorize the conclusion.
静息电位是 K⁺ 外流「攒」出来的，不是 Na⁺。: The resting potential is "built up" by K⁺ outflow, not by Na⁺.
静息时膜主要对 K⁺ 有通透性，K⁺ 外流使膜外阳离子浓度高于膜内，膜两侧表现为: At rest the membrane is mainly permeable to K⁺; K⁺ outflow makes the cation concentration outside higher than inside, so the membrane is negative inside and positive outside. This is the resting potential.
给膜一个刺激，膜电位会怎样变？: Give the membrane a stimulus. How does the membrane potential change?
把「电刺激」拨到「刺激中」，看膜电位与离子: Switch "Electrical stimulus" to "Stimulating" and watch the membrane potential and ions
Na⁺ 从膜外涌进膜内，膜电位由 −70 mV 升到 +30 mV（内正外负），: Na⁺ rushes in from outside, the membrane potential rises from −70 mV to +30 mV (positive inside, negative outside), then falls back; peak reading +30 mV
兴奋：Na⁺ 内流 → 内正外负: Excited: Na⁺ flows in → positive inside, negative outside
受刺激时细胞膜对 Na⁺ 的通透性增加，Na⁺ 内流。: When stimulated, the cell membrane becomes more permeable to Na⁺, and Na⁺ flows in.
这个部位出现暂时性的电位变化，表现为内正外负的兴奋状态。: This region shows a temporary potential change, an excited state that is positive inside and negative outside.
此时的膜电位称为动作电位；邻近未兴奋部位仍是内负外正。: This membrane potential is called the action potential; neighboring unexcited regions are still negative inside and positive outside.
去掉 Na⁺ 通道：怎么刺激都不再出现动作电位——麻药与毒素就是这样起作用的。: Without Na⁺ channels, no stimulus produces an action potential any more; that's how anesthetics and toxins work.
内负外正 ↔ 内正外负，翻过来靠的是 Na⁺ 内流。: Negative inside/positive outside ↔ positive inside/negative outside: the flip comes from Na⁺ inflow.
受刺激时膜对 Na⁺ 通透性增加、Na⁺ 内流，该部位出现内正外负的兴奋状态，此: When stimulated, the membrane becomes more permeable to Na⁺ and Na⁺ flows in; the region becomes excited, positive inside and negative outside, and this membrane potential is called the action potential.
兴奋是怎样沿神经纤维一段一段传下去的？: How is excitation passed down the nerve fiber section by section?
看几秒：兴奋带怎样一段一段往前推，后方怎样恢复: Watch for a few seconds: how the excited band pushes forward section by section, and how the region behind recovers
兴奋带沿轴突一段一段往前推进，后方逐段恢复；剖开后能看到兴奋部位与未兴奋部位之间: The excited band moves along the axon section by section while the region behind recovers in turn; cut open, you can see local current arrows between excited and unexcited regions; the main reading (meter) follows with two deflections
向前传导，后方恢复静息: Conducted forward, the region behind returns to rest
兴奋部位与未兴奋部位之间存在电位差，电荷移动形成局部电流。: There's a potential difference between excited and unexcited regions, and the moving charge forms local currents.
局部电流又刺激相近的未兴奋部位发生同样的电位变化。: Local currents in turn stimulate nearby unexcited regions to undergo the same potential change.
如此进行下去，兴奋向前传导，后方又恢复为静息电位。: And so on: the excitation is conducted forward, and the region behind returns to the resting potential.
去掉局部电流：兴奋走不出受刺激的那一点。: Without local currents, excitation can't get beyond the point that was stimulated.
传导不是「电沿导线流」，而是「一段一段重新兴奋」。: Conduction isn't "electricity flowing along a wire" but "re-excitation section by section".
兴奋部位与未兴奋部位之间的电位差形成局部电流；局部电流刺激相近的未兴奋部位兴奋，: The potential difference between excited and unexcited regions forms local currents, which stimulate nearby unexcited regions, so excitation is conducted forward and the region behind returns to rest.
兴奋怎样跨过两个神经元之间的缝隙？: How does excitation cross the gap between two neurons?
在 3D 里点一下突触小体（杯状的那一团）: Tap the synaptic knob (the cup-shaped mass) in 3D
突触小泡移向前膜并融合，递质被释放到突触间隙、扩散到后膜与受体结合，后膜电位随即: Synaptic vesicles move to the presynaptic membrane and fuse with it, transmitter is released into the cleft, diffuses to the postsynaptic membrane and binds to receptors, and the postsynaptic potential changes (−70 → −55 mV, lesson setting)
相邻的两个神经元并不是直接接触的。: Two neighboring neurons don't actually touch.
突触由突触前膜、突触间隙与突触后膜构成；轴突末梢处有许多突触小泡。: A synapse consists of the presynaptic membrane, synaptic cleft and postsynaptic membrane; the axon terminal holds many synaptic vesicles.
递质由小泡释放、扩散过间隙、与后膜受体结合，引发后膜电位变化；随后被降解或回收。: Transmitter is released from vesicles, diffuses across the cleft and binds to postsynaptic receptors, causing a potential change; it is then broken down or taken back up.
去掉突触小泡：没有递质，信号传不到下一个神经元。: Without synaptic vesicles there's no transmitter, and the signal can't reach the next neuron.
图 2-8 的五步：到达 → 释放 → 扩散 → 结合 → 降解或回收。: The five steps of Fig. 2-8: arrive → release → diffuse → bind → break down or reuptake.
突触由突触前膜、突触间隙与突触后膜构成；递质由突触小泡释放、扩散过间隙、与后膜受: A synapse consists of the presynaptic membrane, synaptic cleft and postsynaptic membrane; transmitter released from synaptic vesicles diffuses across the cleft and binds to postsynaptic receptors, changing the postsynaptic membrane potential.
为什么兴奋只能单向传，而且比在纤维上慢？: Why can excitation only cross in one direction, and more slowly than along a fiber?
看几秒：递质从哪一侧出现，后膜又要过多久才起变化: Watch for a few seconds: which side the transmitter appears from, and how long before the postsynaptic membrane changes
间隙里的递质全部来自突触前膜一侧，后膜一侧一个都没有；后膜电位比「兴奋到达前膜」: All the transmitter in the cleft comes from the presynaptic side, none from the postsynaptic side; the postsynaptic potential starts changing 0.5 physiological ms (0.05 s on screen) after excitation reaches the presynaptic membrane
递质只能由突触前膜释放: Transmitter can only be released by the presynaptic membrane
递质只存在于突触小泡中，只能由突触前膜释放，然后作用于突触后膜上。: Transmitter exists only in synaptic vesicles, can only be released by the presynaptic membrane, and then acts on the postsynaptic membrane.
突触处要经过化学信号的转换（有延搁），单位距离上比在神经纤维上慢得多。: A synapse requires conversion to a chemical signal (with a delay), so per unit distance it's much slower than a nerve fiber.
去掉这条：学生会以为突触能双向传，选择题必错。: Without this point, students think synapses can transmit both ways and will get the multiple-choice question wrong.
单向看「递质从哪侧出现」；「慢」看「延搁有多长」。: One-way: look at "which side the transmitter appears from"; slower: look at "how long the delay is".
把「可卡因」拨到「已加」，看间隙里的多巴胺和受体: Switch "Cocaine" to "Added" and watch the dopamine in the cleft and the receptors
转运蛋白不再回收多巴胺，间隙多巴胺停在 60 % 上不下来（界面 1.5 s 后: Transporter proteins stop taking dopamine back up, and dopamine in the cleft stays at 60 % without falling (still 60 % after 1.5 s on screen); postsynaptic receptors drop from 100 % to about 65 % (a long-term change compressed into seconds, illustrative)
这类物质对神经系统的影响，作用位点往往在突触。: Substances like this usually act on the nervous system at the synapse.
正常时多巴胺发挥作用后，会被突触前膜上的转运蛋白回收。: Normally, after dopamine acts, it's taken back up by transporter proteins on the presynaptic membrane.
可卡因使转运蛋白失去回收多巴胺的功能：多巴胺留在间隙持续发挥作用，导致后膜上的多: Cocaine stops the transporter proteins from taking dopamine back up: dopamine stays in the cleft and keeps acting, which reduces dopamine receptors on the postsynaptic membrane (the real loss of receptors takes days to weeks; it's compressed into seconds on screen, illustrative).
去掉这条：只记住「毒品有害」，说不出为什么「戒不掉」。: Without this point, students only remember "drugs are harmful" and can't say why they're "hard to quit".
错误操作＝「吸一口」；后果＝多巴胺滞留、受体减少；请解释：为什么停药后更难受？: Wrong action = "taking a hit"; consequence = dopamine lingers, receptors decrease; explain: why does stopping make you feel worse?
可卡因使突触前膜上的转运蛋白失去回收多巴胺的功能，多巴胺留在突触间隙持续发挥作用: Cocaine stops the transporter proteins on the presynaptic membrane from taking dopamine back up, so dopamine stays in the synaptic cleft and keeps acting, which reduces dopamine receptors on the postsynaptic membrane; once the effect wears off the receptors are already fewer, so the user has to keep taking the drug, a vicious circle.
降低膜外 Na⁺ 浓度，动作电位会怎样变？: Lower the external Na⁺ concentration. How does the action potential change?
把膜外 Na⁺ 浓度往低处拖（100 % → 70 % 以下），盯住峰值和静息电: Drag the external Na⁺ concentration down (100 % → below 70 %) and watch the peak and the resting potential
峰值随膜外 Na⁺ 降低而降低：100 % 时 +30.0 mV、70 % 时: The peak falls as external Na⁺ falls: +30.0 mV at 100 %, +22.6 mV at 70 %, +19.4 mV at 60 %, +15.6 mV at 50 %; the resting potential stays −70 mV; try the 150 % end yourself (+38.5 mV)
动作电位幅度随膜外 Na⁺ 降低而降低: Action potential amplitude falls as external Na⁺ falls
改变轴突外 Na⁺ 浓度，静息电位并不受影响。: Changing the Na⁺ concentration outside the axon doesn't affect the resting potential.
动作电位的幅度会随着 Na⁺ 浓度的降低而降低。: The action potential's amplitude falls as the Na⁺ concentration falls.
峰值的幅度跟着膜外与膜内 Na⁺ 的浓度差走，而静息电位由 K⁺ 外流决定（教材: The peak amplitude follows the Na⁺ concentration difference between outside and inside, while the resting potential is set by K⁺ outflow (the textbook only says "falls as the concentration falls"; don't remember it as "proportional").
去掉这条：学生会以为膜外 Na⁺ 高低对兴奋没有影响。: Without this point, students think the level of external Na⁺ has no effect on excitation.
同一个滑块，一个读数变、一个读数不变——这就是教材拓展应用 1 的实验结论。: One slider, one reading changes and one doesn't: that's the experimental conclusion of the textbook's extension application 1.
改变轴突外 Na⁺ 浓度，静息电位并不受影响，但动作电位的幅度会随着 Na⁺ 浓: Changing the Na⁺ concentration outside the axon doesn't affect the resting potential, but the action potential's amplitude falls as the Na⁺ concentration falls.
考核：把动作电位恢复成正常: Assessment: restore the action potential to normal
让峰值回到 +28.9 mV 以上并保持 15 秒（中途膜外 Na⁺ 会被抽掉一: Bring the peak back above +28.9 mV and hold for 15 seconds (external Na⁺ will be drained once partway through)
达标横幅；中途膜外 Na⁺ 被抽到 60 %、峰值掉到 +19.4 mV，要自己: Pass banner; partway through external Na⁺ is drained to 60 % and the peak drops to +19.4 mV, and you must drag Na⁺ back yourself
峰值要回到 +28.9 mV 以上：膜外 Na⁺ 不能太低，通道也不能被阻断。: To get the peak back above +28.9 mV, external Na⁺ can't be too low and the channels can't be blocked.
静息电位不受膜外 Na⁺ 影响，看它是不是 −70 mV 就知道膜片是否安静。: The resting potential isn't affected by external Na⁺; check that it's −70 mV to know whether the membrane patch is quiet.
阻断 Na⁺ 通道就没有动作电位——这是麻药与毒素的作用方式。: Block the Na⁺ channels and there's no action potential; that's how anesthetics and toxins act.
没有新内容：前八步的开关和滑块都用上就能达标。: Nothing new: using the switches and sliders from the first eight steps is enough to pass.
考核没有新内容：会看读数、会拨开关、知道哪一条影响峰值。: Nothing new in the assessment: read the readings, flip the switches, and know which factor affects the peak.
考核没有新结论：把膜外 Na⁺ 调回 100 %、保持刺激、解除阻断，动作电位就: The assessment has no new conclusion: set external Na⁺ back to 100 %, keep stimulating, remove the block, and the action potential returns to normal.
停止刺激：膜回到静息状态: Stimulus stopped: the membrane returns to rest
已阻断 Na⁺ 通道：不再出现动作电位: Na⁺ channels blocked: no more action potentials
已加可卡因（示意）：转运蛋白不再回收多巴胺: Cocaine added (illustrative): transporter proteins stop taking dopamine back up
换成正常条件：多巴胺被转运蛋白回收: Back to normal conditions: dopamine is taken back up by transporter proteins

膜外 Na⁺ 被抽掉了：峰值掉到 +19.4 mV: External Na⁺ was drained: the peak dropped to +19.4 mV
把动作电位恢复到正常并保持: Restore the action potential to normal and hold it
整体 · 神经纤维、膜片、突触: Overview · nerve fiber, membrane patch, synapse
神经纤维处于静息状态时，膜两侧的电位是: When a nerve fiber is at rest, the potential across the membrane is
静息时 K⁺ 外流使膜外阳离子浓度高于膜内，膜两侧表现为内负外正（p.28）。: At rest, K⁺ outflow makes the cation concentration outside higher than inside, so the membrane is negative inside and positive outside (p.28).
神经纤维受刺激产生动作电位时，主要是: When a nerve fiber is stimulated and produces an action potential, the main event is
受刺激时膜对 Na⁺ 通透性增加、Na⁺ 内流，表现为内正外负（p.28）。: When stimulated, the membrane becomes more permeable to Na⁺ and Na⁺ flows in, making it positive inside and negative outside (p.28).
兴奋在神经元之间只能单向传递，原因是: Excitation can only pass between neurons in one direction because
突触后膜上没有受体: There are no receptors on the postsynaptic membrane
突触间隙太宽，递质过不去: The synaptic cleft is too wide for transmitter to cross
突触后膜不能产生电位变化: The postsynaptic membrane can't change its potential
递质只存在于突触小泡中，只能由突触前膜释放: Transmitter exists only in synaptic vesicles and can only be released by the presynaptic membrane
递质只存在于突触小泡中、只能由突触前膜释放，然后作用于突触后膜上（p.29）。: Transmitter exists only in synaptic vesicles, can only be released by the presynaptic membrane, and then acts on the postsynaptic membrane (p.29).
降低轴突外 Na⁺ 浓度后: After lowering the Na⁺ concentration outside the axon
动作电位幅度升高，静息电位不受影响: The action potential amplitude rises; the resting potential is unaffected
动作电位幅度降低，静息电位不受影响: The action potential amplitude falls; the resting potential is unaffected
教材拓展应用 1：改变轴突外 Na⁺ 浓度，静息电位并不受影响，但动作电位的幅度: Textbook extension application 1: changing the Na⁺ concentration outside the axon doesn't affect the resting potential, but the action potential's amplitude falls as the Na⁺ concentration falls (p.31).
看懂静息电位、动作电位、局部电流与突触传递，会判断哪些条件会改变动作电位。: Understand the resting potential, action potential, local currents and synaptic transmission, and judge which conditions change the action potential.
示意声明：三个单元均为示意放大；电位数值为课件设定（教材本节未印数值）；时程已放: Disclaimer: all three units are schematic close-ups; potential values are lesson settings (this textbook section prints no values); timing is slowed down (1 physiological ms = 0.1 s on screen); the loss of receptors is a long-term process compressed into seconds (illustrative).
